title: Steady Skies, Tense Region
overview: Regional security stories dominate today — from the fallout of the US-Iran war to a death sentence for Bashar al-Assad — but daily life in Türkiye stays largely on its usual track: the lira holds near 47.7 to the dollar, and Ankara's diplomatic and legislative machinery keeps moving. Residents should note continuing tension in the wider region, especially around the Red Sea and Gulf, even as Türkiye itself remains calm.
body: The US-Iran war remains the backdrop to much regional news. Houthi forces struck a ship carrying Saudi military equipment in the Red Sea, killing several crew — their first deadly attack since the war began — and Reuters and The Economist report additional missile activity in the Gulf. Multiple international outlets (NYT, AP, NBC, Sky News) report that President Trump left Turkey via an unusual security routine after a summit, citing an Iran-linked threat; Turkish and international coverage both note the story but frame it mainly as a US security matter rather than a Turkey-specific one. For residents, this is a reminder to keep half an eye on regional shipping and travel advisories — Iran, Iraq, Syria, and Lebanon remain at the US State Department's highest advisory level (L4), while Türkiye stays at L2.
